ok i have a half-baked handover doc from a previous session:

  Handover

  Goal (COR-389 + your follow-ups): consolidate the two auth views, get the CLI fully onto the context-aware/JWT model, and ultimately auto-refresh JWTs on every control-plane call. Broadly: make auth/login UX coherent.

  Where we got to — shipped in #1341:
  - Auth command surface trimmed from 7 → 5: dropped auth list + auth revoke.
  - auth status is now context-aware: profile via /me on the active context's core, shows identity + active context. auth use finally retargets it.
  - auth contexts → styled table. logout revokes server-side via entire-core (--all = all sessions on the core).
  - Burned all ent_ PAT machinery — the CLI never used PATs; that surface is being sunset.

  Key thing we learned (the expensive lesson): there are two same-shaped "auth/tokens" surfaces — entire-core /api/auth/tokens (login sessions) vs entire.io /api/v1/auth/tokens (legacy ent_ PATs). The CLI was wrongly hitting the PAT one for "sessions" → empty lists + logout 400s. Everything now targets entire-core.
  Full write-up in the COR-389 Linear comment (corrected) and memory auth-token-surfaces.

  What's NOT done (next session):
  1. The actual COR-389 deliverable — silent JWT refresh on control-plane calls (contextTokenStore + RefreshPath into defaultManager). Untouched. This is the real prize; everything so far was prerequisite + cleanup.
  2. Multi-core retargeting for the rest of the control plane — org/repo/project/grant (via coreapi.New()) still use static AuthBaseURL. Only auth status was retargeted. Same bug pattern as the one we just fixed.

  Verification gaps: Go lint clean, per-package tests green; full mise run test:ci (integration + canary) not run. None of it exercised against a live core — please sanity-check entire auth status / logout against your local eu.auth.entire.io.


what i want us to work on todya is making sure that any time we hit an upstream URL from this cli, we use the same mechanism to discover which "auth context" to use (as in contexts.json).

for example, 'entire activity' currently has ENV vars so that i can do this:

18:49:25 $ ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=https://partial.to ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://us.auth.partial.to  entire activity

however, what i'd prefer, is to be able to call 'ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=https://partial.to entire activity' and have it automatically know to use the us.auth.partial.to auth context.

i'm thinking that what we'll need is for https://partial.to to expose /.well-known/entire-auth.json too, just like entire-server does (see ~/src/entirehq/entiredb/cmd/entire-server) to say "i'll accept auth from login servers [au.auth.partial.to, us.auth.partial.to]".  

this might not all make sense - push back and/or ask questions as needed, and we'll go from there.  i'm expecting we'll audit all API calls the cli makes, and see how big a blast radius it'd be to switch over to the new "contexts.json" mechanism.

aiTitle: Implement context-aware auth discovery for CLI API calls

content.text:
Perfect! Now I have enough information to provide a comprehensive report. Let me compile the complete map:

## Auth-Context Mechanism — Complete Map

Based on my thorough investigation of the codebase, here is the complete picture of the auth-context mechanism:

### 1. The contexts.json Model and Storage

**File Location:**
- Default: `~/.config/entire/contexts.json` (customizable via `$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`)
- Path resolution: `/Users/paul/.claude/worktrees/cli/polymorphic-hatching-elephant/internal/entireclient/contexts/contexts.go:59-76`

**Data Structure:**
The `File` struct (contexts.go:46-55) holds:
```go
type File struct {
    CurrentContext string        // Active login name (empty until first login)
    Contexts       []*Context    // Ordered list of stored credentials
}

type Context struct {
    Name             string  // User-facing identifier, defaults to issuer hostname
    CoreURL          string  // JWT issuer URL (what STS exchanges hit) — from token's `iss` claim
    Handle           string  // Principal handle from /api/auth/token response
    KeychainService  string  // OS-keyring slot for the access token
}
```

**File Format & Safety:**
- Line 12: File invariants: 0600 perms, atomic temp+rename writes, exclusive flock under load
- Lock mechanism: `lockFile()` (contexts.go:220-237) — 5-second timeout with 100ms backoff
- Shared by both CLIs: `entirely` and `entiredb` can both read/write contexts.json

**Load & Save:**
- `Load()` (contexts.go:78-92): Reads under exclusive flock, returns empty `File{}` on first run
- `Save()` (contexts.go:96-107): Atomic temp+rename under exclusive flock
- `Modify()` (contexts.go:195-218): Read-modify-write in single locked operation — prevents races

### 2. The "Active Context" & Context Selection

**Resolution:**
- Stored in `CurrentContext` field of contexts.json
- Read by `auth.Contexts()` (contexts.go:112-118): Returns `(all, currentName, error)`
- Selected by user via `entire auth use <name>` → `SetCurrentContext()` (context_store.go:94-108)

**Key Functions:**
- `CurrentContextToken()` (context_store.go:16-30): Returns login JWT for active context, or ("", false)
- `LoginTokenForContext(c *Context)` (contexts.go:207-223): Fetches raw token from keyring slot `c.KeychainService`/`c.Handle`, strips expiry encoding
- `RemoveCurrentContext()` (context_store.go:35-55): Deletes active context + its keyring tokens, clears `CurrentContext`
- `RemoveContext(name)` (context_store.go:61-76): Removes named context + tokens; if it was current, clears `CurrentContext` (never auto-switches)

**Token Lookup with Fallback (`ContextStore`)** (context_store.go:131-157):
Wraps legacy `Store` with context preference:
- `GetToken(baseURL)`: Prefers active context's token, falls back to legacy entry at `baseURL`
- `LoadTokens(profile)`: Returns active context's `TokenSet`, fallback to legacy
- Production use: `auth.NewContextStore()` plugged into `resolveStatusTarget()` and `defaultManager()`

### 3. Base URL Resolution: Auth vs API

**Environment Variables (api/base_url.go:24-30):**
- `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL`: Overrides data API origin (default: `https://entire.io`)
- `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL`: Overrides auth/login origin (default: `https://us.auth.entire.io`)

**URL Resolution Functions (api/base_url.go):**
- `BaseURL()` (38-44): Returns `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` or `DefaultBaseURL`
- `AuthBaseURL()` (59-65): Returns normalized `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` or `DefaultAuthBaseURL`
- `NormalizeOriginURL()` (131-156): Canonicalizes URLs (lowercased scheme/host, default ports stripped, path/query/fragment dropped)
- `OriginOnly()` (162-164): Backwards-compatible alias for `NormalizeOriginURL()`
- `IsSplitHost()` (74-76): Checks if auth and data origins differ

**Critical Invariant (AuthBaseURL docstring:51-58):**
Both values are normalized identically so keys stored in the keyring match what the tokenmanager probes. Without this, `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://AUTH.example.com:443/` would save under the raw form but the manager would normalize to `https://auth.example.com`, causing "not logged in" errors.

### 4. Token Store & JWT Refresh Machinery

**Token Storage Backends (cmd/entire/cli/auth/store.go & tokenstore package):**

**Legacy Single-Entry Store (store.go:30-150):**
- `SaveToken(baseURL, token)`: Persists at keyring service `entire-cli`, key = `baseURL`
- `GetToken(baseURL)`: Retrieves from `entire-cli`/`baseURL`
- `DeleteToken(baseURL)`: Removes from keyring
- Backend selection via env vars:
  - Default: OS keyring (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, etc.)
  - Set `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file` for JSON file backend at `~/.config/entire/tokens.json`

**Keyring Service Naming Convention (tokenstore/tokenstore.go:32-59):**
- `entire-core:<coreURL>`: entire-core control-plane tokens (what contexts.json uses)
- `<service>:refresh`: Paired refresh-token slot for an access-token service
- Example: Access at `entire-core:https://us.auth.entire.io` + refresh at `entire-core:https://us.auth.entire.io:refresh`

**Token Expiration Encoding (tokenstore/expiry.go):**
- Format: `"<token>|<unix_expiry_timestamp>"`
- `EncodeTokenWithExpiration(token, expiresIn)` (21-24): Encodes with TTL
- `DecodeTokenWithExpiration(encoded)` (29-41): Extracts token and `time.Time`
- `IsTokenExpiredOrExpiring(expiresAt)` (45-50): Checks with 5-minute buffer

**Per-Context Token Store (auth/refresh.go:24-105):**
The `contextTokenStore` struct (34-37) adapts one login context's keyring slots to auth-go's `tokenstore.Store`:
- Access token at `(service, handle)` with expiry encoding
- Refresh token raw at `(service:refresh, handle)`
- Implements `LoadTokens()`, `SaveTokens()`, `DeleteTokens()` for tokenmanager

**Refresh Token Sequencing (refresh.go:65-97):**
Critical safety rule: Refresh token persisted **before** access token.
- Single-use rotation means failed refresh write aborts before access token touched (old pair preserved)
- Failed access write after good refresh self-heals on next load

**Tokenmanager Integration (auth/exchange.go:78-112):**
- `defaultManager()` (78-112): Built once at process startup via `sync.Once`
- Config:
  - `Issuer`: `api.AuthBaseURL()` (normalized)
  - `ClientID`: From `CurrentProvider()` (typically `"entire-cli"`)
  - `STSPath`: From `CurrentProvider()` (v1: empty, v2: `"/oauth/token"`)
  - `Store`: `NewContextStore()` — context-preferring store
  - `UserAgent`: Provider's ClientID
  - `AllowInsecureHTTP`: Allows loopback http:// or set by `EnableInsecureHTTP()`
- Env override: `ENTIRE_AUTH_PROVIDER_VERSION` (v1 or v2)

**Provider Resolution (auth/provider.go:63-107):**
- v1 (legacy single-host): `ClientID="entire-cli"`, `TokenPath="/oauth/token"`, `STSPath=""` (same-host always wins)
- v2 (OIDC split-host): `ClientID="entire-cli"`, `DeviceCodePath="/device_authorization"`, `TokenPath="/oauth/token"`, `STSPath="/oauth/token"`
- Auto-detect: `IsSplitHost()` true → v2; collapsed → v1
- Override: `ENTIRE_AUTH_PROVIDER_VERSION` env var

**Token For Resource (auth/exchange.go:118-124):**
`TokenForResource(ctx, resourceBaseURL)` performs RFC 8693 token exchange when needed:
- Same-origin shortcut: Stored core token returned unchanged, no STS exchange
- Different origin: STS endpoint exchanges core token for resource-scoped token

### 5. auth status Context-Aware Resolution (PR #1341)

**Key Pattern (cmd/entire/cli/auth.go:161-183):**

```go
// newAuthStatusCmd() calls:
target := resolveStatusTarget(auth.NewContextStore(), auth.Contexts, api.AuthBaseURL())
return runAuthStatus(..., target)
```

**resolveStatusTarget() Logic (auth.go:223-242):**
1. Load all contexts and active name via `listContexts()` (injection point)
2. If active context exists with non-empty `CoreURL`:
   - Try `LoginTokenForContext(c)` to get session token
   - Return `statusTarget{coreURL: c.CoreURL, token: tok, activeContext: c.Name}`
3. Fallback: Use legacy entry at `fallbackBaseURL` (typically `api.AuthBaseURL()`)
4. Return structure (statusTarget):
   ```go
   type statusTarget struct {
       coreURL       string  // The core to query (active context's CoreURL or fallback)
       token         string  // Session JWT for that core
       activeContext string  // Name if context, "" if legacy fallback
       totalContexts int     // Count of saved contexts
   }
   ```

**How Auth Status Uses It (auth.go:278-320):**
1. `defaultFetchProfile(ctx, target.coreURL, target.token)`: GET `/me` on active context's core (or fallback)
2. `defaultListAuthSessions(ctx, target.coreURL, target.token)`: List active sessions on the same core
3. Render profile + session table + context name if active
4. Show multi-context hint if more than one context exists

**Session Endpoint (api/auth_sessions.go:1-101):**
- Path: `/api/auth/tokens` (coreAuthSessionsPath in auth.go)
- Client: `NewClientWithBaseURL(token, coreURL).WithAuthSessionsPath(path)`
- Methods: `ListAuthSessions()`, `RevokeCurrentAuthSession()`, `RevokeAuthSession(id)`
- Response: `AuthSession` with ID, Name, Scope, CreatedAt, LastUsedAt, ExpiresAt

**Pattern for Control-Plane Commands:**
- Old (before PR #1341): All hit `api.AuthBaseURL()` statically
- New: Call `resolveStatusTarget()` to get context's core, then hit that core with context's token
- Example: `logout` uses same target as `auth status` (logout.go:76, 82-87)

**Warning on Cross-Core Switch (auth_context.go:46-71):**
`warnIfCrossCoreContext()` detects when `auth use` switches to a different core:
- Compares `c.CoreURL` vs `api.AuthBaseURL()` via `api.OriginOnly()`
- Warns that control-plane commands still target the configured auth host (not yet retargetable)
- Git clone still works because it resolves per-cluster

### 6. Login & Context Recording

**RecordLoginContext() Flow (contexts.go:47-117):**
1. Parse token claims to extract `iss` (issuer/CoreURL), `handle` (or fallback to `sub`)
2. Pick context name via `pickContextName()` (126-146):
   - Reuse existing name if (CoreURL, handle) pair already exists
   - Prefer bare hostname (`contextNameForCoreURL()`)
   - If taken, qualify as `handle@host`
   - If still taken, use numeric suffix
3. Store tokens in keyring:

```go

    CurrentContext string        // Active login name (empty until first login)
    Contexts       []*Context    // Ordered list of stored credentials

    Name             string  // User-facing identifier, defaults to issuer hostname

    Handle           string  // Principal handle from /api/auth/token response
    KeychainService  string  // OS-keyring slot for the access token

```

**File Format & Safety:**
- Line 12: File invariants: 0600 perms, atomic temp+rename writes, exclusive flock under load
- Lock mechanism: `lockFile()` (contexts.go:220-237) — 5-second timeout with 100ms backoff
- Shared by both CLIs: `entirely` and `entiredb` can both read/write contexts.json

**Load & Save:**
- `Load()` (contexts.go:78-92): Reads under exclusive flock, returns empty `File{}` on first run
- `Save()` (contexts.go:96-107): Atomic temp+rename under exclusive flock
- `Modify()` (contexts.go:195-218): Read-modify-write in single locked operation — prevents races

**Resolution:**
- Stored in `CurrentContext` field of contexts.json
- Read by `auth.Contexts()` (contexts.go:112-118): Returns `(all, currentName, error)`
- Selected by user via `entire auth use <name>` → `SetCurrentContext()` (context_store.go:94-108)

- `LoginTokenForContext(c *Context)` (contexts.go:207-223): Fetches raw token from keyring slot `c.KeychainService`/`c.Handle`, strips expiry encoding
- `RemoveCurrentContext()` (context_store.go:35-55): Deletes active context + its keyring tokens, clears `CurrentContext`
- `RemoveContext(name)` (context_store.go:61-76): Removes named context + tokens; if it was current, clears `CurrentContext` (never auto-switches)

**Token Lookup with Fallback (`ContextStore`)** (context_store.go:131-157):
Wraps legacy `Store` with context preference:
- `GetToken(baseURL)`: Prefers active context's token, falls back to legacy entry at `baseURL`
- `LoadTokens(profile)`: Returns active context's `TokenSet`, fallback to legacy

- `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL`: Overrides data API origin (default: `https://entire.io`)
- `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL`: Overrides auth/login origin (default: `https://us.auth.entire.io`)

- `BaseURL()` (38-44): Returns `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` or `DefaultBaseURL`

- `OriginOnly()` (162-164): Backwards-compatible alias for `NormalizeOriginURL()`
- `IsSplitHost()` (74-76): Checks if auth and data origins differ

Both values are normalized identically so keys stored in the keyring match what the tokenmanager probes. Without this, `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://AUTH.example.com:443/` would save under the raw form but the manager would normalize to `https://auth.example.com`, causing "not logged in" errors.

1	package clusterdiscovery
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"net/http"
8		"sort"
9		"strings"
10	
11		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/contexts"
12		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/discovery"
13	)
14	
15	// ResolveContextForCluster picks the local login context to authenticate
16	// git operations against clusterHost.
17	//
18	// It separates two concerns that used to be conflated in a single
19	// cluster→context binding:
20	//
21	//   - Which control plane(s) front the cluster — an objective infra fact.
22	//     Discovered from the cluster's /.well-known/entire-cluster.json and
23	//     cached in cluster_cores.json (see discovery.ClusterCoresCache) with
24	//     a long TTL, since a cluster's home core is near-static. On a cache
25	//     miss or expiry we re-fetch; if the re-fetch fails we fall back to
26	//     the stale cached cores rather than break the op.
27	//
28	//   - Which of the user's accounts to use — recomputed every call from the
29	//     live contexts, never persisted. So a user with several accounts is
30	//     never silently pinned to one identity.
31	//
32	// Account selection (selectContext):
33	//
34	//  1. If the active context (current_context) is issued by one of the
35	//     cluster's cores, use it. This is the explicit lever: `entire auth
36	//     use <name>` chooses the identity for every cluster that context's
37	//     core fronts.
38	//  2. Otherwise gather every local context eligible for the cluster (its
39	//     CoreURL is among the advertised cores):
40	//     - exactly one  → use it (the common single-account case);
41	//     - none         → error with the login hint listing the cluster's cores;
42	//     - more than one → error asking the user to pick with `entire auth use`,
43	//     rather than silently guessing an account.
44	//
45	// We never fall back to an active context whose core does NOT front the
46	// cluster: the cluster would reject the exchanged token as "unknown
47	// cluster_host", and silently authenticating a staging identity against a
48	// prod cluster (or vice versa) is exactly the confusion the /.well-known
49	// lookup exists to prevent.
50	//
51	// debugf is optional; nil suppresses debug output.
52	func ResolveContextForCluster(ctx context.Context, configDir, cacheDir, clusterHost string, httpClient *http.Client, debugf DebugFunc) (*contexts.Context, error) {
53		if debugf == nil {
54			debugf = func(string, ...any) {}
55		}
56		f, err := contexts.Load(configDir)
57		if err != nil {
58			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load contexts: %w", err)
59		}
60	
61		coreURLs, err := resolveClusterCores(ctx, cacheDir, clusterHost, httpClient, debugf)
62		if err != nil {
63			return nil, err
64		}
65	
66		return selectContext(f, clusterHost, coreURLs, debugf)
67	}
68	
69	// ResolveClusterCores returns the trusted control-plane core URLs that
70	// front clusterHost, using the same cache-then-/.well-known discovery as
71	// ResolveContextForCluster (see resolveClusterCores). Exported for callers
72	// that need the cluster's trusted-core set without account selection — e.g.
73	// the ENTIRE_TOKEN path validates that the env token's audience is one of
74	// these before exchanging it, so an unverified JWT can't redirect the
75	// token exchange to an attacker-chosen host.
76	func ResolveClusterCores(ctx context.Context, cacheDir, clusterHost string, httpClient *http.Client, debugf DebugFunc) ([]string, error) {
77		if debugf == nil {
78			debugf = func(string, ...any) {}
79		}
80		return resolveClusterCores(ctx, cacheDir, clusterHost, httpClient, debugf)
81	}
82	
83	// resolveClusterCores returns the control-plane core URLs that front
84	// clusterHost, from cluster_cores.json when fresh, otherwise via a live
85	// /.well-known fetch (which is then cached). A stale-but-present cache
86	// entry is used as a fallback when the live fetch fails, so a brief
87	// cluster outage doesn't break an operation whose cores we already knew.
88	func resolveClusterCores(ctx context.Context, cacheDir, clusterHost string, httpClient *http.Client, debugf DebugFunc) ([]string, error) {
89		cache, err := discovery.LoadClusterCores(cacheDir)
90		if err != nil {
91			// A cache read problem must not block resolution — discover live.
92			debugf("cluster-cores cache load failed: %v; discovering live", err)
93			cache = nil
94		}
95	
96		var stale []string
97		if cache != nil {
98			if urls, fresh, ok := cache.Get(clusterHost); ok {
99				if fresh {
100					debugf("cluster %s cores from cache: %v", clusterHost, urls)
101					return urls, nil
102				}
103				stale = urls
104				debugf("cluster %s cores cache expired; re-fetching /.well-known", clusterHost)
105			}
106		}
107	
108		body, err := Discover(ctx, clusterHost, httpClient, debugf)
109		if err != nil {
110			if stale != nil {
111				debugf("discovery for %s failed (%v); falling back to stale cached cores %v", clusterHost, err, stale)
112				return stale, nil
113			}
114			return nil, formatDiscoveryError(clusterHost, err)
115		}
116	
117		if mErr := discovery.ModifyClusterCores(cacheDir, func(c discovery.ClusterCoresCache) error {
118			c.Set(clusterHost, body.CoreURLs)
119			return nil
120		}); mErr != nil {
121			// Non-fatal: we resolved the cores, the next call just re-fetches.
122			debugf("cluster-cores cache write for %s failed: %v", clusterHost, mErr)
123		}
124		return body.CoreURLs, nil
125	}
126	
127	// selectContext applies the account-selection rules over the cluster's
128	// advertised cores. See ResolveContextForCluster for the rationale.
129	func selectContext(f *contexts.File, clusterHost string, coreURLs []string, debugf DebugFunc) (*contexts.Context, error) {
130		eligible := eligibleContexts(f, coreURLs)
131	
132		// 1. Active context wins when it's eligible for this cluster.
133		if current := f.Find(f.CurrentContext); current != nil {
134			for _, c := range eligible {
135				if c.Name == current.Name {
136					debugf("cluster %s -> active context %s", clusterHost, current.Name)
137					return current, nil
138				}
139			}
140		}
141	
142		// 2. Otherwise the eligible set decides.
143		switch len(eligible) {
144		case 0:
145			return nil, errors.New(RenderLoginHint(clusterHost, coreURLs))
146		case 1:
147			debugf("cluster %s -> sole eligible context %s", clusterHost, eligible[0].Name)
148			return eligible[0], nil
149		default:
150			return nil, ambiguousContextError(clusterHost, eligible)
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// eligibleContexts returns the local contexts whose core is among coreURLs,
155	// de-duplicated by name. Order is unspecified — callers either use the sole
156	// element or report the whole set, never index [0] as a silent winner.
157	func eligibleContexts(f *contexts.File, coreURLs []string) []*contexts.Context {
158		seen := make(map[string]bool)
159		var out []*contexts.Context
160		for _, coreURL := range coreURLs {
161			for _, c := range f.ContextsForIssuer(coreURL) {
162				if !seen[c.Name] {
163					seen[c.Name] = true
164					out = append(out, c)
165				}
166			}
167		}
168		return out
169	}
170	
171	// ambiguousContextError is returned when more than one local context could
172	// authenticate against the cluster and none is active. We refuse to guess —
173	// the user picks explicitly. Names are sorted so the message is stable.
174	func ambiguousContextError(clusterHost string, eligible []*contexts.Context) error {
175		names := make([]string, len(eligible))
176		for i, c := range eligible {
177			names[i] = c.Name
178		}
179		sort.Strings(names)
180		return fmt.Errorf("multiple login contexts can authenticate against cluster %s (%s); choose one with `entire auth use <context>` and re-run",
181			clusterHost, strings.Join(names, ", "))
182	}
183	
184	// formatDiscoveryError turns a Discover error into the message
185	// operators have always seen at this layer. Kept here (not on the
186	// sentinels themselves) so the package's errors stay machine-readable
187	// while the caller-facing strings remain centralised.
188	func formatDiscoveryError(clusterHost string, err error) error {
189		switch {
190		case errors.Is(err, ErrUnreachable):
191			return fmt.Errorf("%s doesn't look like a cluster, or it is unreachable: %w", clusterHost, err)
192		case errors.Is(err, ErrNoIssuers):
193			return fmt.Errorf("cluster %s does not advertise any trusted login servers (HTTP 503 from %s); contact the cluster administrator",
194				clusterHost, Path)
195		case errors.Is(err, ErrNoCoreURLs):
196			return fmt.Errorf("cluster %s advertises no trusted core URLs (empty list at %s); contact the cluster administrator",
197				clusterHost, Path)
198		default:
199			return fmt.Errorf("cluster discovery for %s: %w", clusterHost, err)
200		}
201	}
202

content.text:
Done auditing. Here's the bottom line before we pick a direction.

## Bottom line

**The mechanism you're describing already exists — you don't need a new `/.well-known/entire-auth.json`, and entire-server likely needs zero changes.** The blast radius is a *wiring* job in the CLI, not new protocol/server work. Two facts change the framing:

1. **The discovery endpoint already exists**: `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` on the data plane returns `core_urls` (the login/core servers it accepts auth from) — exactly your "I'll accept auth from [au/us.auth.partial.to]" idea. There's also `/.well-known/entire-federation` on cores for cross-region peers.
2. **The CLI already has the full resolver** in `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery`: `ResolveContextForCluster(host) → *contexts.Context`. Given a data host, it fetches+caches the well-known, reads `core_urls`, and picks the login context whose `CoreURL` matches (active-context-wins → sole-eligible → error on zero/ambiguous). **`git-remote-entire` already uses this for every clone/push.** The main CLI commands just don't.

So `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=https://partial.to entire activity` auto-discovering `us.auth.partial.to` is `ResolveContextForCluster("partial.to")` — which is written, tested, and shipping. We're lifting it into the rest of the CLI.

## Audit: who resolves hosts how

| Resolution | Commands | Count |
|---|---|---|
| **Already context-aware** | `git-remote-entire` (clone/push), `auth status`, `logout` | — |
| Static `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` (core/control-plane, via `coreapi.New()`) | `org`, `repo`, `project`, `grant`, `login` | ~13 sites |
| Static `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` (data plane) | `activity`, `trail`, `search`, `dispatch` | ~11 sites |
| Hardcoded external (fine, ignore) | version-check (GitHub), telemetry (PostHog) | 2 |

**Inflection points**: ~24 call sites funnel through ~5 constructors (`coreapi.New`, `NewAuthenticatedAPIClient`, `auth.NewClient`, dispatch `NewCloudClient`, `search.Search`). Retarget those 5 and everything downstream follows.

## The one real risk

The default no-env case: **does prod `entire.io` actually serve `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` advertising `us.auth.entire.io`?** The endpoint is implemented on the entiredb data-plane server, but if the prod `entire.io` deployment doesn't serve it, discovery breaks for normal users and we need a static fallback. That's an ops fact I can't verify from this repo.

A few forks decide how much we bite off. Let me get your calls:

Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. Let me compile my findings:

## Summary of entire.io API Server Analysis

Based on my thorough search of the `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io` reference repository, here are my findings:

### 1. **NO `/.well-known/*` Endpoint Exists**

Grep results confirm entire.io serves **no discovery endpoints** at all:
- `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/env.ts:118` - Only references to `.well-known` are comments describing that entire-core's JWKS is served at `/.well-known/jwks.json`
- `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/lib/core-jwt.ts:61` - The code *fetches* JWKS from upstream: `createRemoteJWKSet(new URL(\`${baseUrl}/.well-known/jwks.json\`)`

**entire.io itself serves NO discovery endpoint** and does not advertise which login/auth/core servers it trusts.

### 2. **Authentication Mechanism: JWT Validation from entire-core**

entire.io authenticates incoming CLI requests via **Bearer token JWT validation**:

**File: `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/lib/middleware.ts:180-259`**
- **Function**: `requireBearerAuth` middleware
- **Two token types supported**:
  1. **API Tokens** (`ent_*` prefix): Stored locally in PlanetScale, validated via hash lookup (lines 200-230)
  2. **entire-core JWTs**: Validated via remote JWKS fetch (lines 233-259)

**File: `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/lib/core-jwt.ts`**
- **JWT Verification** (lines 144-240):
  - Fetches JWKS from: `${ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL}/.well-known/jwks.json` (line 61)
  - **Algorithm**: EdDSA (pinned, line 153)
  - **Required Claims** (lines 154-156):
    - `iss`: Must equal `ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL` (configured issuer)
    - `aud`: Must match `ENTIRE_CORE_JWT_AUDIENCE` (configured audience)
  - **Scope Enforcement** (lines 224-226): JWT must carry `entire:api-access` scope
  - **Subject Validation** (lines 174-196): Must contain GitHub provider info (`provider=github`, numeric `provider_user_id`)

**Configuration Environment Variables** (from `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/env.ts:118-123`):
```
ENTIRE_CORE_BEARER_ENABLED?       // Feature flag to enable JWT validation
ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL?              // Base URL of the trust root IdP (e.g., us.auth.partial.to)
ENTIRE_CORE_JWT_AUDIENCE?          // Expected 'aud' claim (e.g., "entire-web-api")
```

### 3. **Trust Roots: Multiple Issuers with Regional Support**

entire.io supports **multi-region/multi-issuer trust** via configuration:

**File: `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/env.ts:121`**
```
ENTIRE_CORE_TRUSTED_ISSUERS?: string 
// Comma-separated allowlist of regional auth hosts permitted as RFC 9207 `iss` on /auth/core/callback 
// (e.g. "https://us.auth.partial.to,https://eu.auth.partial.to"); 
// ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL is implicitly trusted
```

**File: `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/routes/auth.ts:118-138`** (`resolveCoreTokenEndpoint` function):
- Validates that `iss` claim (if present) is either:
  - Matches configured `ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL` (default/implicit trust), OR
  - Is in the operator-configured `ENTIRE_CORE_TRUSTED_ISSUERS` allowlist
- Rejects unknown issuers to prevent client_secret leakage

### 4. **Protected Routes via Bearer Auth**

These routes require JWT validation via `requireBearerAuth`:

**File: `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/app.ts:357-382` (route mounting)**

Routes protected under `/api/v1`:
- `/api/v1/me/commits` - Bearer auth required
- `/api/v1/me/activity` - Bearer auth required  
- `/search/v1/search` - Bearer auth (separate search-worker app at `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/search-worker/index.ts:41`)
- `/api/v1/dispatches/generate` - Bearer auth required (mounted at line 364)
- `/api/v1/trails/*` - Bearer auth + optional session (codeReviewRoutes mounted line 378)

**Search endpoint** (`/search/v1/search`): Handled in separate Cloudflare Worker (`search-worker`), validates JWT identically (files 8-9, 233-251 of search-worker/index.ts).

### 5. **Multi-Cluster/Region Support**

entire.io has **awareness of multiple clusters/regions** but **no discovery endpoint**:

**File: `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/env.ts:125`**
```
ENTIRE_DB_PREFERRED_CLUSTER?: string 
// Optional preferred cluster host; when a repo is mirrored to multiple 
// clusters this one wins, otherwise the first match from core /api/v1/mirrors is used
```

**File: `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/routes/entire-core.ts`**
- `/api/v1/entire/mirrors` endpoint lists user's mirrors with `clusterHost` field
- Clusters are resolved dynamically from entire-core's `/api/v1/mirrors` API (not self-advertised)

### 6. **HTTP Route Surface**

**Root level handlers** (from `/Users/paul/src/entirehq/entire.io/api/src/app.ts:394-462`):
- `GET /api/health` - Unprotected health check (lines 200-226)
- `GET /api/status` - Unprotected status with endpoint map (lines 229-355)
- `GET /api/openapi.json` - OpenAPI schema (lines 394-399)
- `GET /api/docs` - Scalar UI for API docs (lines 401-459)
- `GET /auth/start`, `GET /auth/*/callback` - OAuth redirects (lines 391-392)
- `POST /oauth/token`, `POST /oauth/device/code` - OAuth token endpoints (lines 391-392)
- **404 handler** for all undefined routes (line 462)

**NO root-level `/` handler** and **NO `/.well-known/*` handlers** exist.

### 7. **Authentication Enforcement Pattern**

Routes follow this pattern:
- Routes under `/api/v1` mounted via `v1.route()` (lines 360-381)
- Runner routes apply wildcard `requireAuth` middleware (runners.ts line 2): `runnerRoutes.use("*", requireAuth)`
- Bearer-specific routes (me, trails) explicitly use `requireBearerAuth` middleware
- Session-only routes use `requireAuth` (session cookie + CSRF)

### Conclusion

**entire.io currently has NO discovery endpoint and would need one added** (analogous to entiredb's `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json`). The design is:

1. **Single-issuer focused**: Configured via `ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL` + `ENTIRE_CORE_JWT_AUDIENCE`
2. **Multi-issuer capable**: Via `ENTIRE_CORE_TRUSTED_ISSUERS` allowlist for regional auth hosts
3. **Statically configured**: Trust roots are environment variables, not advertised via HTTP
4. **JWKS delegation**: Fetches signing keys from upstream entire-core's `/.well-known/jwks.json`

To add discovery (like entiredb), you'd implement `GET /.well-known/entire-api.json` (or similar) returning:
```json
{
  "issuer": "https://us.auth.partial.to",
  "trusted_issuers": ["https://us.auth.partial.to", "https://eu.auth.partial.to"],
  "jwks_uri": "https://us.auth.partial.to/.well-known/jwks.json",
  "audience": "entire-web-api"
}
```

Now I've got the distinction right. Corrected model:

**Three upstream families, not one:**

| Family | Repo | Hit by | Discovery today |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cluster** (git data plane) | entiredb / entire-server | `git-remote-entire` | ✅ serves `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` (`core_urls`); CLI already resolves it via `clusterdiscovery` |
| **Core** (control plane) | entire-core | `org`/`repo`/`project`/`grant` via `coreapi.New()` → `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` | host *is* the core — no discovery needed; context = the one whose `CoreURL` == host |
| **API** (data plane) | **entire.io** (staging = partial.to) | `activity`/`search`/`trail`/`dispatch` via `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` | ❌ **no well-known**; this is the gap |

So your original instinct was right, just aimed at the wrong repo: **entire.io is the one that needs to grow a `.well-known`.** It already *knows* its trusted login servers — they're static config (`ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL` + `ENTIRE_CORE_TRUSTED_ISSUERS` allowlist, e.g. `us.auth.partial.to,eu.auth.partial.to`) and it expects a specific audience (`ENTIRE_CORE_JWT_AUDIENCE`, e.g. `entire-web-api`). It just doesn't *advertise* any of it. entiredb's `entire-cluster.json` only carries `core_urls` — for entire.io the CLI also needs the **audience** to know what to token-exchange for, so the API blob likely needs to be richer than the cluster one.

The CLI-side resolver (`ResolveContextForCluster`) is reusable in shape, but it's hardwired to the cluster path/JSON. The unifying job: one "host → trusted issuers → pick context → mint right-audience token" path, with the *source* of trusted issuers varying per family (cluster.json / new api.json / the core itself).

15	// apiBasePath is appended to the control-plane origin to reach the v1
16	// surface. The generated spec's single server entry is "/api/v1", so the
17	// origin we dial is <core-host> and the client base is <core-host>/api/v1.
18	const apiBasePath = "/api/v1"
19	
20	// New returns a *Client wired to talk to the Entire control plane (Core
21	// API) as the currently logged-in user.
22	//
23	// The base URL is the auth/login host — the Core API is served at
24	// <auth-host>/api/v1, and that host is exactly what `entire login`
25	// authenticated against, so no extra configuration is needed. Override
26	// with ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL for non-default deployments (the same knob
27	// `entire login` honours).
28	//
29	// Auth is the logged-in bearer, resolved lazily per request through
30	// auth.TokenForResource so an RFC 8693 token exchange happens
31	// transparently when the stored token's audience doesn't already cover
32	// the control-plane host.
33	func New() (*Client, error) {
34		base := strings.TrimRight(api.AuthBaseURL(), "/")
35		// The token exchange's resource must be the bare origin; api.OriginOnly
36		// strips any path/query so the audience the manager keys on matches
37		// what the server expects.
38		src := &bearerSource{resourceBaseURL: api.OriginOnly(base)}
39		client, err := NewClient(base+apiBasePath, src)
40		if err != nil {
41			return nil, fmt.Errorf("build core API client: %w", err)
42		}
43		return client, nil
44	}
45	
46	// NewWithBearer returns a *Client targeting an explicit core origin with a
47	// fixed bearer token — no per-request resolution or STS exchange. Used when a
48	// command must hit a specific login server rather than the configured
49	// AuthBaseURL: e.g. `entire auth status` querying /me on the active context's
50	// core with that context's session token.
51	func NewWithBearer(coreBaseURL, token string) (*Client, error) {
52		base := strings.TrimRight(coreBaseURL, "/")
53		client, err := NewClient(base+apiBasePath, staticBearer{token: token})
54		if err != nil {
55			return nil, fmt.Errorf("build core API client: %w", err)
56		}
57		return client, nil
58	}

60	// staticBearer is a SecuritySource that returns a fixed bearer token. Same
61	// sessionAuth-skipping rationale as bearerSource.
62	type staticBearer struct{ token string }
63	
64	func (s staticBearer) BearerAuth(context.Context, OperationName) (BearerAuth, error) {
65		return BearerAuth{Token: s.token}, nil
66	}
67

69		return SessionAuth{}, ogenerrors.ErrSkipClientSecurity
70	}

73	// logged-in user's bearer token for every request. The control plane
74	// only uses bearerAuth from the CLI; the sessionAuth (browser cookie)
75	// scheme is reported as ErrSkipClientSecurity so ogen's middleware
76	// satisfies the "bearerAuth OR sessionAuth" requirement via the bearer
77	// alone — without adding a stray `Cookie: entire_session=` header.
78	// (Returning an empty SessionAuth would not skip the cookie: the
79	// generated securitySessionAuth unconditionally calls req.AddCookie.)
80	type bearerSource struct {
81		resourceBaseURL string
82	}

84	func (b *bearerSource) BearerAuth(ctx context.Context, _ OperationName) (BearerAuth, error) {
85		token, err := auth.TokenForResource(ctx, b.resourceBaseURL)
86		if err != nil {
87			// Only suggest login when the user genuinely isn't logged in.
88			// Other failures (STS rejection, network, malformed config) must
89			// surface verbatim rather than be masked by a login hint.
90			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {

100		// session cookie. ErrSkipClientSecurity tells ogen to drop this
101		// scheme entirely for the request (no Cookie header added); the
102		// bearerAuth path alone satisfies the OR-requirement.
103		return SessionAuth{}, ogenerrors.ErrSkipClientSecurity
104	}

117		var statusErr *ErrorModelStatusCode
118		if !errors.As(err, &statusErr) {
119			return ""
120		}

88			m, err := tokenmanager.New(tokenmanager.Config{
89				Issuer:   issuer,
90				ClientID: provider.ClientID,

116	// stored core token's audience doesn't already cover that resource.
117	// See tokenmanager.Manager.Token for the full resolution rules.
118	func TokenForResource(ctx context.Context, resourceBaseURL string) (string, error) {

126	// isLoopbackHTTP reports whether u is an http:// URL pointing at a
127	// loopback hostname (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1). Used to scope the
128	// "auto-permit insecure HTTP" path on the tokenmanager so production
129	// misconfigurations fail loudly while loopback-only local-dev flows
130	// keep working.
131	func isLoopbackHTTP(rawURL string) bool {
132		u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
133		if err != nil || u.Scheme != "http" {
134			return false
135		}
136		host := u.Hostname()
137		return host == "localhost" || host == "127.0.0.1" || host == "::1"
138	}

content.text: The singleton manager is pinned to `AuthBaseURL()` as issuer — so for a context on a *different* core, both the token store preference and the STS host would be wrong. There's already per-context manager machinery in `refresh.go`. Let me read it and the context store.

content.content:
1	package auth
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"net/http"
8		"strings"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/tokenmanager"
12		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/tokens"
13		authtokenstore "github.com/entireio/auth-go/tokenstore"
14	
15		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/contexts"
16		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/tokenstore"
17	)
18	
19	// defaultSavedTokenTTL is the encoded keychain expiry used when a refreshed
20	// token carries no usable ExpiresAt. The server is the real authority; this
21	// only governs when local readers consider the cached token stale.
22	const defaultSavedTokenTTL = time.Hour
23	
24	// contextTokenStore adapts one login context's keyring slots to auth-go's
25	// tokenstore.Store, so tokenmanager can load, refresh, and persist that
26	// context's credentials. It is bound to a specific (service, handle) at
27	// construction and ignores the profile argument: the cluster resolver has
28	// already chosen exactly one context, so there is no per-issuer account
29	// ambiguity to resolve here.
30	//
31	// Access token lives at `service`/`handle` (with the "|<expiry>" encoding
32	// the rest of the CLI reads); the refresh token lives raw at
33	// `service:refresh`/`handle`.
34	type contextTokenStore struct {
35		service string
36		handle  string
37	}
38	
39	func (s contextTokenStore) LoadTokens(string) (tokens.TokenSet, error) {
40		enc, err := tokenstore.Get(s.service, s.handle)
41		// Map "no credential stored" to auth-go's sentinel so tokenmanager
42		// reports "not logged in" rather than a hard store failure.
43		if errors.Is(err, tokenstore.ErrNotFound) || (err == nil && enc == "") {
44			return tokens.TokenSet{}, authtokenstore.ErrNotFound
45		}
46		if err != nil {
47			return tokens.TokenSet{}, fmt.Errorf("read access token: %w", err)
48		}
49		access, expiresAt := tokenstore.DecodeTokenWithExpiration(enc)
50		// A missing refresh slot is fine (login predating offline_access) — treat
51		// it as no-refresh. Any other store error must surface, not be swallowed:
52		// dropping it would silently discard a valid refresh token and force a
53		// re-login on what was really a transient keyring/file-store failure.
54		refresh, err := tokenstore.Get(tokenstore.RefreshService(s.service), s.handle)
55		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, tokenstore.ErrNotFound) {
56			return tokens.TokenSet{}, fmt.Errorf("read refresh token: %w", err)
57		}
58		return tokens.TokenSet{
59			AccessToken:  access,
60			RefreshToken: refresh,
61			ExpiresAt:    expiresAt,
62		}, nil
63	}
64	
65	func (s contextTokenStore) SaveTokens(_ string, t tokens.TokenSet) error {
66		if t.AccessToken == "" {
67			return errors.New("save tokens: empty access token")
68		}
69		expiresIn := int64(defaultSavedTokenTTL.Seconds())
70		if !t.ExpiresAt.IsZero() {
71			if secs := int64(time.Until(t.ExpiresAt).Seconds()); secs > 0 {
72				expiresIn = secs
73			}
74		}
75		// Persist the rotated refresh token BEFORE the access token. The server
76		// single-use-rotates refresh tokens, so a partial write must never leave
77		// a fresh access token paired with a stale refresh token: that pairing
78		// looks healthy until the access token expires, then the dead refresh
79		// token trips invalid_grant/family revocation and forces a re-login.
80		// Refresh-first inverts the failure modes: a failed refresh write aborts
81		// before touching the access slot (old pair preserved), and a failed
82		// access write after a good refresh write self-heals on the next load
83		// (the new refresh token re-mints an access token).
84		//
85		// persistRefreshed carries a still-valid refresh token forward when the
86		// server doesn't rotate, so an empty value here means "leave as-is",
87		// never "clear".
88		if t.RefreshToken != "" {
89			if err := tokenstore.Set(tokenstore.RefreshService(s.service), s.handle, t.RefreshToken); err != nil {
90				return fmt.Errorf("store refresh token: %w", err)
91			}
92		}
93		if err := tokenstore.Set(s.service, s.handle, tokenstore.EncodeTokenWithExpiration(t.AccessToken, expiresIn)); err != nil {
94			return fmt.Errorf("store access token: %w", err)
95		}
96		return nil
97	}
98	
99	func (s contextTokenStore) DeleteTokens(string) error {
100		_ = tokenstore.Delete(tokenstore.RefreshService(s.service), s.handle) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort; the access-token delete below is what matters
101		if err := tokenstore.Delete(s.service, s.handle); err != nil {
102			return fmt.Errorf("delete access token: %w", err)
103		}
104		return nil
105	}
106	
107	// NewRefreshingLoginProvider returns a login-JWT provider (the shape
108	// repocreds wants) for context c that transparently re-mints an expired
109	// login JWT from the stored refresh token.
110	//
111	// It is backed by auth-go's tokenmanager, which is what makes this safe
112	// against the server's single-use refresh-token rotation: refreshes are
113	// serialised across processes (an advisory file lock) and goroutines, the
114	// store is re-read after locking so a late waiter reuses a peer's freshly
115	// minted token, and the rotated refresh token is persisted. Without that,
116	// two concurrent git-remote-entire processes (e.g. a recursive submodule
117	// fetch) could replay the same single-use token and trip the server's
118	// reuse detection, revoking the whole family.
119	//
120	// Behaviour is a strict superset of the old read-only provider: a still
121	// valid token is returned with no network call; a context with no refresh
122	// token (e.g. a login predating offline_access) behaves exactly as before
123	// — valid token used, expired token surfaces a re-login error.
124	//
125	// transport carries the caller's TLS configuration; allowInsecureHTTP
126	// permits an http:// core for loopback/dev.
127	func NewRefreshingLoginProvider(c *contexts.Context, transport http.RoundTripper, allowInsecureHTTP bool) (func(context.Context) (string, error), error) {
128		if c == nil {
129			return nil, errors.New("nil context")
130		}
131		if c.KeychainService == "" || c.Handle == "" {
132			return nil, fmt.Errorf("context %q has no keychain slot", c.Name)
133		}
134		mgr, err := tokenmanager.New(tokenmanager.Config{
135			Issuer:            strings.TrimRight(c.CoreURL, "/"),
136			ClientID:          CurrentProvider().ClientID,
137			RefreshPath:       CurrentProvider().TokenPath,
138			Store:             contextTokenStore{service: c.KeychainService, handle: c.Handle},
139			Transport:         transport,
140			AllowInsecureHTTP: allowInsecureHTTP,
141			UserAgent:         CurrentProvider().ClientID,
142		})
143		if err != nil {
144			return nil, fmt.Errorf("init token manager for context %q: %w", c.Name, err)
145		}
146		name := c.Name
147		coreURL := strings.TrimRight(c.CoreURL, "/")
148		// Name the core in the re-login hint so a multi-core user logs back
149		// into the right one; matches clusterdiscovery.RenderLoginHint's idiom.
150		relogin := fmt.Sprintf("ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=%s entire login", coreURL)
151		return func(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
152			tok, err := mgr.Refresh(ctx)
153			switch {
154			case errors.Is(err, tokenmanager.ErrReauthRequired):
155				return "", fmt.Errorf("login session for %q (%s) expired; run `%s` to re-authenticate", name, coreURL, relogin)
156			case errors.Is(err, tokenmanager.ErrNotLoggedIn):
157				return "", fmt.Errorf("no usable login for %q (%s); run `%s`", name, coreURL, relogin)
158			case err != nil:
159				return "", fmt.Errorf("refresh login token: %w", err)
160			}
161			return tok, nil
162		}, nil
163	}

1	package api
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"net/url"
7		"os"
8		"strings"
9	)
10	
11	// ErrInsecureHTTP is returned when the base URL uses HTTP without an explicit opt-in.
12	var ErrInsecureHTTP = errors.New("refusing to use insecure http:// base URL for authentication (use --insecure-http-auth to override)")
13	
14	const (
15		// DefaultBaseURL is the production Entire API origin.
16		DefaultBaseURL = "https://entire.io"
17	
18		// DefaultAuthBaseURL is the production Entire auth origin (device flow,
19		// auth-token management, keyring key). The CLI is split-host by default:
20		// auth on us.auth.entire.io, data on entire.io.
21		DefaultAuthBaseURL = "https://us.auth.entire.io"
22	
23		// BaseURLEnvVar overrides the Entire API origin for local development.
24		BaseURLEnvVar = "ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL"
25	
26		// AuthBaseURLEnvVar overrides only the auth/login origin (device flow,
27		// auth-tokens management, keyring key). Falls back to DefaultAuthBaseURL
28		// when unset; local-dev and single-host deployments must set this
29		// alongside ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL.
30		AuthBaseURLEnvVar = "ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL"
31	
32		schemeHTTP  = "http"
33		schemeHTTPS = "https"
34	)
35	
36	// BaseURL returns the effective Entire API base URL.
37	// ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL takes precedence over the production default.
38	func BaseURL() string {
39		if raw := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(BaseURLEnvVar)); raw != "" {
40			return normalizeBaseURL(raw)
41		}
42	
43		return DefaultBaseURL
44	}
45	
46	// AuthBaseURL returns the origin used for the device-flow login, auth-token
47	// management endpoints, and the keyring key under which the bearer token is
48	// stored. ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL takes precedence; otherwise it falls back to
49	// DefaultAuthBaseURL (split-host by default).
50	//
51	// The result is canonicalised — lowercased scheme/host, default port stripped,
52	// path/query/fragment dropped, trailing slash collapsed — so the value that
53	// flows into store.SaveToken keys matches what tokenmanager.New emits after
54	// its own NormalizeOriginURL pass. Without this, a user setting
55	// ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://AUTH.example.com:443/ would log in successfully
56	// (saved under the raw form) but every subsequent data-API command would
57	// resolve "not logged in" because the manager probes under the normalised
58	// "https://auth.example.com".
59	func AuthBaseURL() string {
60		raw := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(AuthBaseURLEnvVar))
61		if raw == "" {
62			raw = DefaultAuthBaseURL
63		}
64		return NormalizeOriginURL(raw)
65	}
66	
67	// IsSplitHost reports whether the CLI is configured for split-host —
68	// i.e. ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL points at a different origin than the data
69	// API. Both sides are canonicalised via NormalizeOriginURL before
70	// comparison: AuthBaseURL already does this internally, but BaseURL
71	// only trims whitespace and a trailing slash, so a cosmetically-
72	// different ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL (uppercase host, explicit :443, path
73	// suffix) would otherwise look split when it isn't.
74	func IsSplitHost() bool {
75		return AuthBaseURL() != NormalizeOriginURL(BaseURL())
76	}
77	
78	// ResolveURL joins an API-relative path against the effective base URL.
79	func ResolveURL(path string) (string, error) {
80		return ResolveURLFromBase(BaseURL(), path)
81	}
82	
83	// ResolveURLFromBase joins an API-relative path against an explicit base URL.
84	// Only http and https schemes are accepted.
85	func ResolveURLFromBase(baseURL, path string) (string, error) {
86		base, err := url.Parse(baseURL)
87		if err != nil {
88			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse base URL: %w", err)
89		}
90	
91		if base.Scheme != schemeHTTP && base.Scheme != schemeHTTPS {
92			return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported base URL scheme %q (must be http or https)", base.Scheme)
93		}
94	
95		rel, err := url.Parse(path)
96		if err != nil {
97			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse path: %w", err)
98		}
99	
100		return base.ResolveReference(rel).String(), nil
101	}
102	
103	// RequireSecureURL returns ErrInsecureHTTP if the base URL uses the http scheme.
104	// Call this before making authenticated requests unless --insecure-http-auth is set.
105	func RequireSecureURL(baseURL string) error {
106		u, err := url.Parse(baseURL)
107		if err != nil {
108			return fmt.Errorf("parse base URL: %w", err)
109		}
110	
111		if u.Scheme == schemeHTTP {
112			return ErrInsecureHTTP
113		}
114	
115		return nil
116	}
117	
118	func normalizeBaseURL(raw string) string {
119		return strings.TrimRight(strings.TrimSpace(raw), "/")
120	}
121	
122	// NormalizeOriginURL canonicalises an origin URL the same way auth-go's
123	// tokenmanager does internally: lowercase scheme/host, default port stripped
124	// (80 for http, 443 for https), path/query/fragment dropped, trailing slash
125	// collapsed. On parse failure, raw is returned unchanged so non-URL audience
126	// values still compare byte-for-byte.
127	//
128	// Mirrors auth-go's internal/oauthhttp.NormalizeOriginURL so the value the
129	// CLI hands to the manager as Issuer survives the manager's own normalisation
130	// pass byte-for-byte — see AuthBaseURL.
131	func NormalizeOriginURL(raw string) string {
132		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
133		u, err := url.Parse(trimmed)
134		if err != nil || u.Scheme == "" || u.Host == "" {
135			return trimmed
136		}
137		scheme := strings.ToLower(u.Scheme)
138		hostname := strings.ToLower(u.Hostname())
139		port := u.Port()
140		dropPort := port == "" ||
141			(scheme == schemeHTTP && port == "80") ||
142			(scheme == schemeHTTPS && port == "443")
143	
144		out := url.URL{Scheme: scheme}
145		switch {
146		case dropPort && strings.Contains(hostname, ":"):
147			out.Host = "[" + hostname + "]"
148		case dropPort:
149			out.Host = hostname
150		case strings.Contains(hostname, ":"):
151			out.Host = "[" + hostname + "]:" + port
152		default:
153			out.Host = hostname + ":" + port
154		}
155		return out.String()
156	}
157	
158	// OriginOnly is a backwards-compatible alias for NormalizeOriginURL.
159	// Callers reading raw URLs (e.g. ENTIRE_SEARCH_URL) and feeding them into
160	// tokenmanager.TokenRequest.Resource use this to strip path/query/fragment
161	// before the lib's stricter origin-only validator runs.
162	func OriginOnly(raw string) string {
163		return NormalizeOriginURL(raw)
164	}

**The seam**: every `org`/`repo`/`project`/`grant` command funnels through `runCore` → `coreapi.New()`, which is hardwired to `AuthBaseURL()` (the default `us.auth.entire.io`) and resolves its token via the singleton manager pinned to that same issuer. 2. `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()` — precedence: explicit env → today's static path (unchanged); else active context → its `CoreURL` + a per-context refreshing token source; else → static default.
3. `coreapi` gets a token-func SecuritySource; `New()` consults the resolver.

message.content: wait a sec, "three-family model"?  That sounds crazy.  Which 3 do we mean?

content.text:
Fair — "three families" is the wrong framing and I muddied it. There aren't three auth systems. There's **one identity model and a set of resource servers**. Let me restate cleanly:

**One identity provider (the "core" / login server):** `entire-core` (e.g. `us.auth.entire.io`). This is what mints your JWT, what `contexts.json` is keyed on (`CoreURL`), and — co-located — it also serves the control-plane CRUD (`/api/v1/orgs`, `repos`, `grants`). An auth context *is* a login to one core.

**Resource servers that trust a core and accept its JWTs:**
- the **git cluster** = `entiredb`/`entire-server` (git-remote-entire hits it)
- the **web/data API** = `entire.io` (`activity`/`search`/`trail`/`dispatch`)

So the "three" I sloppily named were really: **the core** (1 thing, both IdP + control-plane) plus **two resource servers**. The only reason they looked like peers in my audit is that the CLI currently resolves each one's host independently from env vars.

The unifying model you're after is just:
> An auth context = a login to one core. Every upstream call resolves to *some host*; that host either **is** a core (control plane → use the context's `CoreURL` directly) or is a **resource server** that advertises which cores it trusts (via a `.well-known`), so the CLI picks the matching context and exchanges its token for that resource.

- **Cluster** already does this (`entire-cluster.json` → `core_urls` → `clusterdiscovery`).
- **Control plane** needs no discovery — the host *is* the core. ← today's slice.
- **entire.io** is the gap: it needs to grow the same kind of `.well-known` so the CLI can map it back to a core/context.

So today's work is unchanged. I'll fix the design-doc framing to "one core + resource servers," not "three families." Want me to proceed with the build on that framing?

content.text:
**Today = the control-plane slice only.** Concretely:

**What changes:** `org`, `repo`, `project`, `grant` (every command behind `runCore` → `coreapi.New()`). Right now they always dial the static default core (`us.auth.entire.io` unless `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` is set) and resolve the token from a singleton manager pinned to that same host. So if you've `entire auth use`'d a context on a *different* core, these commands silently ignore it — the exact bug pattern your handover flagged.

**The fix:** make `coreapi.New()` resolve its host + token from the **active context** instead of the static default. Since the control-plane host *is* the core, there's no `.well-known` discovery here — just "use the active context's `CoreURL` and its token." Precedence:
1. `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` explicitly set → unchanged (override wins).
2. else active context → its `CoreURL` + a **per-context refreshing** token source (this is where silent JWT refresh lands for the control plane — a down payment on COR-389, reusing the existing `NewRefreshingLoginProvider`).
3. else → static default (today's behavior for users who never ran `auth use`).

**Deliverables (the 5 tasks):**
- `api.AuthBaseURLOverridden()` + `auth.insecureHTTPEnabled()` readers
- `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()` — the shared resolver
- rewire `coreapi.New()` through it
- unit tests for precedence + the token-source wiring
- a short design doc in the "one core + resource servers" framing, recording what's deferred

**What today explicitly does NOT touch:**
- **Cluster** (git-remote-entire) — already context-aware, nothing to do.
- **entire.io API family** (`activity`/`search`/`trail`/`dispatch`) — deferred; needs the new `entire-api.json` well-known on your side first + the audience token-exchange. Design only.

Net user-visible effect after today: `entire auth use <ctx>` actually retargets `org`/`repo`/`project`/`grant` to that context's core, and their tokens refresh silently. Want me to build it?

# Upstream Host & Auth-Context Resolution

How the CLI decides *which host to dial* and *which login (auth context) to
authenticate as* for every upstream call. The goal is one mental model:

> An **auth context** is a login to one **core** (the identity provider /
> login server). Every upstream call resolves to some host. That host either
> **is** a core — use the active context's core directly — or it is a
> **resource server** that advertises which cores it trusts via a
> `/.well-known` blob, so the CLI picks the context whose core is trusted and
> exchanges that context's token for the resource.

There is no separate "auth system" per service. There is one identity model
(`contexts.json`, keyed on `CoreURL`) and a set of resource servers that
accept a core's JWTs.

## The pieces

| Role | Service (prod / staging) | Hit by | Trusted-core discovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core** — IdP **and** control-plane API, co-located | `entire-core` (`us.auth.entire.io`) | `org` / `repo` / `project` / `grant`, `auth *`, `login` | none needed — the host *is* the core |
| **Resource: git cluster** | `entire-server` / `entiredb` | `git-remote-entire` (clone/push) | `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` → `core_urls` |
| **Resource: web/data API** | `entire.io` (`partial.to`) | `activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` | **none today** — see [Deferred](#deferred) |

`contexts.json` (`$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR/contexts.json`, shared with entiredb's
CLIs) stores each login as `{Name, CoreURL, Handle, KeychainService}` plus a
`CurrentContext` pointer. `CoreURL` is the JWT `iss` — the core that minted the
token. `entire auth use <ctx>` flips `CurrentContext`.

## Resolution per call type

### Git cluster (done — `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery`)

`ResolveContextForCluster(host)` fetches+caches the cluster's
`/.well-known/entire-cluster.json`, reads `core_urls`, then selects the
context: active-context-wins if its `CoreURL` is among the cores, else the
sole eligible context, else an error (zero → login hint; ambiguous → asks for
`auth use`). The token is then exchanged for the cluster.

### Control plane (done — this slice)

The host *is* a core, so there is no discovery. `coreapi.New()` consults
`auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()`:

1. **`ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` set** → that origin, verbatim; bearer via the
   singleton token manager (`TokenForResource`). The env var is an
   unconditional override, so split-host / local-dev invocations are
   untouched.
2. **else active context** → its `CoreURL`, with a **per-context refreshing**
   bearer (`auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider`): the token manager is keyed on
   `c.CoreURL` as issuer, so store reads and refresh/STS hit the right core,
   and an expired access token is silently re-minted from the stored refresh
   token. This is what makes `entire auth use <ctx>` actually retarget
   `org`/`repo`/`project`/`grant`.
3. **else** (no active context) → the configured default origin +
   `TokenForResource` — the pre-contexts behaviour.

Key files: `cmd/entire/cli/auth/control_plane.go` (resolver),
`cmd/entire/cli/auth/refresh.go` (per-context refreshing provider),
`internal/coreapi/client.go` (`New()` + `providerSource`),

# Upstream Host & Auth-Context Resolution

How the CLI decides *which host to dial* and *which login (auth context) to
authenticate as* for every upstream call. The goal is one mental model:

> An **auth context** is a login to one **core** (the identity provider /
> login server). Every upstream call resolves to some host. That host either
> **is** a core — use the active context's core directly — or it is a
> **resource server** that advertises which cores it trusts via a
> `/.well-known` blob, so the CLI picks the context whose core is trusted and
> exchanges that context's token for the resource.

There is no separate "auth system" per service. There is one identity model
(`contexts.json`, keyed on `CoreURL`) and a set of resource servers that
accept a core's JWTs.

## The pieces

| Role | Service (prod / staging) | Hit by | Trusted-core discovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core** — IdP **and** control-plane API, co-located | `entire-core` (`us.auth.entire.io`) | `org` / `repo` / `project` / `grant`, `auth *`, `login` | none needed — the host *is* the core |
| **Resource: git cluster** | `entire-server` / `entiredb` | `git-remote-entire` (clone/push) | `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` → `core_urls` |
| **Resource: web/data API** | `entire.io` (`partial.to`) | `activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` | **none today** — see [Deferred](#deferred) |

`contexts.json` (`$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR/contexts.json`, shared with entiredb's
CLIs) stores each login as `{Name, CoreURL, Handle, KeychainService}` plus a
`CurrentContext` pointer. `CoreURL` is the JWT `iss` — the core that minted the
token. `entire auth use <ctx>` flips `CurrentContext`.

## Resolution per call type

### Git cluster (done — `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery`)

`ResolveContextForCluster(host)` fetches+caches the cluster's
`/.well-known/entire-cluster.json`, reads `core_urls`, then selects the
context: active-context-wins if its `CoreURL` is among the cores, else the
sole eligible context, else an error (zero → login hint; ambiguous → asks for
`auth use`). The token is then exchanged for the cluster.

### Control plane (done — this slice)

The host *is* a core, so there is no discovery. `coreapi.New()` consults
`auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()`:

1. **`ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` set** → that origin, verbatim; bearer via the
   singleton token manager (`TokenForResource`). The env var is an
   unconditional override, so split-host / local-dev invocations are
   untouched.
2. **else active context** → its `CoreURL`, with a **per-context refreshing**
   bearer (`auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider`): the token manager is keyed on
   `c.CoreURL` as issuer, so store reads and refresh/STS hit the right core,
   and an expired access token is silently re-minted from the stored refresh
   token. This is what makes `entire auth use <ctx>` actually retarget
   `org`/`repo`/`project`/`grant`.
3. **else** (no active context) → the configured default origin +
   `TokenForResource` — the pre-contexts behaviour.

`cmd/entire/cli/auth/refresh.go` (per-context refreshing provider),
`internal/coreapi/client.go` (`New()` + `providerSource`),
`cmd/entire/cli/api/base_url.go` (`AuthBaseURLOverridden`).

(`auth/exchange.go:defaultManager`) is built once with `Issuer =
api.AuthBaseURL()`. When the active context lives on a *different* core, both

That warning is now **stale** — and it's cleanup belonging to *this* work, not the next bit. My change just made it wrong.

Here's the precise situation:
- It claims `org`/`project`/`repo`/`grant` "still target the configured auth host… doesn't retarget them yet." After this slice, they **do** retarget to the active context's core.
- It also lumps in `auth status` — which already retargeted back in #1341, so that part was *already* stale before I touched anything.
- It does **not** mention the data-API commands (`activity`/`search`/`trail`/`dispatch`) — those are the next bit (the entire.io well-known work), and they genuinely still don't follow the context.

So the only case where switching context still *won't* retarget the control plane is when `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` is explicitly set (the override wins by design). The current trigger condition (`c.CoreURL != AuthBaseURL()`) now fires in the common no-override case and tells the user the exact opposite of the truth.

Let me see what the tests pin before I rewrite it.

content.text:
Reading further, your question surfaced a real inconsistency I introduced — worth your call before I "fix" the warning.

**The warning itself is stale.** It says `org`/`project`/`repo`/`grant` (and `auth status`) "don't retarget yet." After this slice they do, and `auth status` already did since #1341. It also never covered the data-API commands (`activity`/`search`/…) — those are the genuinely-still-broken next-bit. So as written it now tells users the opposite of the truth in the common case.

**But here's the snag:** my commit and the existing #1341 code disagree on precedence when `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` *and* an active context are both set and point at different cores:

| Command | My `coreapi.New()` | `auth status` (#1341) |
|---|---|---|
| precedence | **env override wins** | **active context always wins** (env is only the no-context fallback) |

So today, with the override set + a cross-core context, `org list` would hit the override host while `auth status` hits the context's core. That's incoherent.

**The override-wins behavior is also just wrong on reflection:** a token minted by core B doesn't validate against core A, so "use the override host but the context's identity" can't succeed. The only sane reading of an override is "where to talk when I have no context." Local-dev still works either way, because logging in against the override creates a context whose `CoreURL` *is* the override.

My recommendation: **align on "active context wins; `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` is the fallback when there's no context"** (matching `auth status`), then delete `warnIfCrossCoreContext` entirely — once `auth use` authoritatively retargets the control plane, there's nothing to warn about. The data-API caveat gets its own, accurate note when I do that next slice.

# Upstream Host & Auth-Context Resolution

How the CLI decides *which host to dial* and *which login (auth context) to
authenticate as* for every upstream call. The goal is one mental model:

> An **auth context** is a login to one **core** (the identity provider /
> login server). Every upstream call resolves to some host. That host either
> **is** a core — use the active context's core directly — or it is a
> **resource server** that advertises which cores it trusts via a
> `/.well-known` blob, so the CLI picks the context whose core is trusted and
> exchanges that context's token for the resource.

There is no separate "auth system" per service. There is one identity model
(`contexts.json`, keyed on `CoreURL`) and a set of resource servers that
accept a core's JWTs.

## The pieces

| Role | Service (prod / staging) | Hit by | Trusted-core discovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core** — IdP **and** control-plane API, co-located | `entire-core` (`us.auth.entire.io`) | `org` / `repo` / `project` / `grant`, `auth *`, `login` | none needed — the host *is* the core |
| **Resource: git cluster** | `entire-server` / `entiredb` | `git-remote-entire` (clone/push) | `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` → `core_urls` |
| **Resource: web/data API** | `entire.io` (`partial.to`) | `activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` | **none today** — see [Deferred](#deferred) |

`contexts.json` (`$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR/contexts.json`, shared with entiredb's
CLIs) stores each login as `{Name, CoreURL, Handle, KeychainService}` plus a
`CurrentContext` pointer. `CoreURL` is the JWT `iss` — the core that minted the
token. `entire auth use <ctx>` flips `CurrentContext`.

## Resolution per call type

### Git cluster (done — `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery`)

`ResolveContextForCluster(host)` fetches+caches the cluster's
`/.well-known/entire-cluster.json`, reads `core_urls`, then selects the
context: active-context-wins if its `CoreURL` is among the cores, else the
sole eligible context, else an error (zero → login hint; ambiguous → asks for
`auth use`). The token is then exchanged for the cluster.

### Control plane (done — this slice)

The host *is* a core, so there is no discovery. `coreapi.New()` consults
`auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()`:

1. **`ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` set** → that origin, verbatim; bearer via the
   singleton token manager (`TokenForResource`). The env var is an
   unconditional override, so split-host / local-dev invocations are
   untouched.
2. **else active context** → its `CoreURL`, with a **per-context refreshing**
   bearer (`auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider`): the token manager is keyed on
   `c.CoreURL` as issuer, so store reads and refresh/STS hit the right core,
   and an expired access token is silently re-minted from the stored refresh
   token. This is what makes `entire auth use <ctx>` actually retarget
   `org`/`repo`/`project`/`grant`.
3. **else** (no active context) → the configured default origin +
   `TokenForResource` — the pre-contexts behaviour.

Key files: `cmd/entire/cli/auth/control_plane.go` (resolver),
`cmd/entire/cli/auth/refresh.go` (per-context refreshing provider),
`internal/coreapi/client.go` (`New()` + `providerSource`),
`cmd/entire/cli/api/base_url.go` (`AuthBaseURLOverridden`).

Why the per-context path and not the singleton manager: the singleton
(`auth/exchange.go:defaultManager`) is built once with `Issuer =
api.AuthBaseURL()`. When the active context lives on a *different* core, both
its token-store reads and its STS/refresh endpoint are keyed on the wrong
host. The per-context provider fixes that by keying on `c.CoreURL`.

## Deferred: the web/data API (`entire.io`)

`activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` dial `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL`
(default `entire.io`) and statically resolve their token. `entire.io` is a
**resource server** — it validates incoming JWTs against statically-configured
trusted issuers (`ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL` + `ENTIRE_CORE_TRUSTED_ISSUERS`) and a
fixed audience (`ENTIRE_CORE_JWT_AUDIENCE`, e.g. `entire-web-api`) — but it
does **not advertise** any of this. So the CLI can't map an `entire.io` host
back to a core/context the way it does for a git cluster.

To close the gap (so `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=https://partial.to entire activity`
auto-selects the right context without also setting `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL`):

1. **Server**: `entire.io` grows a `/.well-known/entire-api.json` advertising
   its trust roots. Unlike the cluster blob (`core_urls` only), the API blob
   must also carry the **audience** the CLI exchanges for:
   ```json
   {
     "issuer": "https://us.auth.partial.to",
     "trusted_issuers": ["https://us.auth.partial.to", "https://eu.auth.partial.to"],
     "audience": "entire-web-api",
     "jwks_uri": "https://us.auth.partial.to/.well-known/jwks.json"
   }
   ```
2. **CLI**: generalize the cluster resolver into a shared "host → trusted
   issuers → pick context" path whose *source* of trusted issuers is pluggable
   (cluster.json / api.json / the core itself), then exchange the context's
   token for the advertised audience via `auth.TokenForResource`. Wire it into
   the `activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` constructors
   (`NewAuthenticatedAPIClient`, `dispatch.NewCloudClient`, `search.Search`).

`ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` / `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` remain explicit overrides: when
set they short-circuit discovery; discovery only runs when they are unset.

Pushed to `cor-389-control-plane-context-aware`. Here's my suggested PR — **not created yet**, your review first:

---

**Title:** `COR-389: control-plane commands follow the active auth context`

**Body:**

```markdown
`org`/`repo`/`project`/`grant` now authenticate as the **active login context**
instead of always hitting the static default core — and refresh their token
silently.

## Why
After `entire auth use <ctx>`, control-plane commands ignored the switch: they
always dialed `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` (or the `us.auth.entire.io` default) and
resolved their token from a manager pinned to that host. So a context on a
different core was silently unused — the bug pattern `auth status` already fixed
in #1341, now extended to the rest of the control plane.

## What changed
- `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()` picks host + token from the active context,
  falling back to `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL`/default only when no context is active.
  The env var is a **fallback host, not an override** (a token from core B can't
  authenticate against core A), matching `auth status`.
- `coreapi.New()` resolves through it; the bearer comes from the per-context
  refreshing provider, so an expired token re-mints from the stored refresh
  token (the silent-refresh down payment on COR-389).
- Removed the now-stale `auth use` cross-core warning and updated its help.
- `docs/architecture/upstream-host-resolution.md`: the "one core + resource
  servers" model and the deferred data-API work.

## Effect
```
entire auth use <ctx-on-another-core>
entire org list      # now hits that context's core, with a silently-refreshed token
```

## Not in scope (next slice)
Data-API commands (`activity`/`search`/`trail`/`dispatch`) still target
`ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` and don't follow the context yet — that needs a
`/.well-known` on `entire.io` advertising its trusted cores + audience. Designed
in the doc.

## Test
`mise run check` — unit + integration green, lint clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```

---
