1	# Entire - CLI
2	
3	This repo contains the CLI for Entire.
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh
8	
9	## Key Directories
10	
11	### Commands (`cmd/`)
12	
13	- `entire/`: Main CLI entry point. Also home to kubectl-style external-command resolution (`entire <name>` → `entire-<name>` on PATH) — see [External Commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md).
14	- `entire/cli`: CLI utilities and helpers (Cobra commands, helpers, group roots)
15	- `entire/cli/commands`: actual command implementations
16	- `entire/cli/agent`: agent implementations (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi) - see [Agent Integration Checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) and [Agent Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md)
17	- `entire/cli/strategy`: strategy implementation (manual-commit) - see section below
18	- `entire/cli/checkpoint`: checkpoint storage abstractions (temporary and committed)
19	- `entire/cli/session`: session state management
20	- `entire/cli/integration_test`: integration tests (simulated hooks)
21	- `e2e/`: E2E tests with real agent calls (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md))
22	
23	### Command Layout
24	
25	The CLI is organized around five noun groups plus a small set of top-level
26	verbs. The groups are the canonical home for each verb; legacy top-level
27	shortcuts remain functional but hidden, and emit a deprecation hint pointing
28	at the canonical group form.
29	
30	- `session` (alias: `sessions`): `list`, `info`, `stop`, `attach`, `resume`, `current`
31	- `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `explain`, `rewind`, `search`
32	- `agent`: bare opens the interactive agent selector, plus `list`, `add`, `remove`
33	- `configure`: bare prints help and a hint pointing at `entire agent`; flags
34	  manage non-agent settings (telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy
35	  options, summary provider). Agent CRUD lives under `entire agent`.
36	- `auth`: `login`, `logout`, `status`, `contexts`, `use`. `logout` takes
37	  `--everywhere` (revoke every session on the active core, not just the
38	  current one) and `--all-contexts` (log out of every saved login)
39	- `doctor`: bare runs the scan-and-fix flow, plus `trace`, `logs`, `bundle`
40	
41	Top-level lifecycle and standalone commands: `enable`, `disable`, `status`,
42	`login`, `logout`, `clean`, `version`, `dispatch`, `activity`, `help`,
43	`configure`.
44	
45	Hidden top-level shortcuts (functional, emit a one-line deprecation hint):
46	`rewind` → `checkpoint rewind`, `resume` → `session resume`, `attach` →
47	`session attach`, `explain` → `checkpoint explain`, `trace` → `doctor trace`.
48	Cobra-native aliases (no hint): `sessions` → `session`, `cp`/`checkpoints` →
49	`checkpoint`. The `search` top-level remains hidden without a hint.
50	
51	Deprecated top-level alias (functional, prints cobra deprecation message):
52	`reset` → `clean`.
53	
54	Hidden infrastructure commands: `hooks`, `trail`,
55	`curl-bash-post-install`, `__send_analytics`.
56	
57	The `hideAsAlias(cmd, canonical)` helper in `cmd/entire/cli/aliascmd.go`
58	marks a command Hidden and sets cobra's `Deprecated` field so the hint
59	renders to stderr on every invocation while the command stays functional.
60	Diagnostic subcommands live alongside `doctor.go` as `doctor_logs.go` and
61	`doctor_bundle.go`. Group roots and noun-group children live in files
62	named `<noun>_group.go` and `<noun>_<verb>.go` respectively.
63	
64	## Tech Stack
65	
66	- Language: Go 1.26.x
67	- Build tool: mise, go modules
68	- Linting: golangci-lint
69	
70	## Development
71	
72	### Running Tests
73	
74	```bash
75	mise run test
76	```
77	
78	### Running Integration Tests
79	
80	```bash
81	mise run test:integration
82	```
83	
84	### Running All Tests (CI)
85	
86	```bash
87	mise run test:ci
88	```
89	
90	This runs unit tests, integration tests, and the E2E canary (Vogon agent) in sequence. Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.
91	
92	### Running E2E Canary Tests (Vogon Agent)
93	
94	The Vogon agent is a deterministic fake agent that exercises the full E2E test suite without making any API calls.
95	
96	```bash
97	mise run test:e2e:canary           # Run all E2E tests with the Vogon agent
98	mise run test:e2e:canary TestFoo   # Run a specific test
99	```
100	
101	- **Runs as part of `test:ci`** — canary failures block merges
102	- **No API calls, no cost** — safe to run freely, unlike real agent E2E tests
103	- **If a canary test fails, the bug is in the CLI or test infrastructure**, not in an agent
104	- Located in `e2e/vogon/` (binary) and `cmd/entire/cli/agent/vogon/` (Agent interface)
105	- The binary parses prompts via regex, creates/modifies/deletes files, and fires lifecycle hooks
106	- **IMPORTANT: When changing E2E test prompt wording**, the Vogon binary (`e2e/vogon/main.go`) parses prompts with hardcoded regexes. New phrasing may not match existing patterns — always run `mise run test:e2e:canary` after changing prompt text and fix Vogon's parsing if tests fail.
107	
108	### Running E2E Tests (Only When Explicitly Requested)
109	
110	**IMPORTANT: Do NOT run E2E tests proactively.** E2E tests make real API calls to agents, which consume tokens and cost money. Only run them when the user explicitly asks for E2E testing.
111	
112	```bash
113	mise run test:e2e [filter]                          # All agents, filtered
114	mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code [filter]       # Claude Code only as an example here, replace `claude-code` with other agents to run tests for those agents
115	```
116	
117	E2E tests:
118	
119	- Use the `//go:build e2e` build tag
120	- Located in `e2e/tests/`
121	- See [`e2e/README.md`](e2e/README.md) for full documentation (structure, debugging, adding agents)
122	- Test real agent interactions (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi, or Vogon creating files, committing, etc.)
123	- Validate checkpoint scenarios documented in `docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md`
124	- Support multiple agents via `E2E_AGENT` env var (`claude-code`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, `copilot-cli`, `pi`, `vogon`)
125	
126	**Environment variables:**
127	
128	- `E2E_AGENT` - Agent to test with (default: `claude-code`)
129	- `E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` - Claude model to use (default: `haiku` for cost efficiency)
130	- `E2E_TIMEOUT` - Timeout per prompt (default: `2m`)
131	
132	### Test Parallelization
133	
134	**Always use `t.Parallel()` in tests.** Every top-level test function and subtest should call `t.Parallel()` unless it modifies process-global state (e.g., `os.Chdir()`).
135	
136	```go
137	func TestFeature_Foo(t *testing.T) {
138	    t.Parallel()
139	    // ...
140	}
141	
142	// Integration tests with TestEnv
143	func TestFeature_Bar(t *testing.T) {
144	    t.Parallel()
145	    env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
146	    // ...
147	}
148	```
149	
150	**Exception:** Tests that modify process-global state cannot be parallelized. This includes `os.Chdir()`/`t.Chdir()` and `os.Setenv()`/`t.Setenv()` — Go's test framework will panic if these are used after `t.Parallel()`.
151	
152	### Git in Tests
153	
154	**Tests that touch git state must use an isolated temp repo — never the real repo CWD.**
155	
156	Many handlers (lifecycle, strategy, hooks) resolve the git repo from CWD via `OpenRepository`, `GetGitCommonDir`, `DetectFileChanges`, etc. Without isolation, tests can create session state files, shadow branches, or other artifacts in the real `.git/` directory.
157	
158	Use the `testutil` helpers:
159	
160	```go
161	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
162	testutil.InitRepo(t, tmpDir)                    // git init + user config + disable GPG
163	testutil.WriteFile(t, tmpDir, "f.txt", "init")  // create a file
164	testutil.GitAdd(t, tmpDir, "f.txt")             // stage it
165	testutil.GitCommit(t, tmpDir, "init")           // commit (needs at least one commit for HEAD)
166	t.Chdir(tmpDir)                                 // redirect CWD-based git resolution
167	```

// completeContextNames is the ValidArgsFunction for commands taking a single
// <context> positional. It offers the stored context names, each annotated
// (shell-completion descriptions, after a tab) with handle, core URL, and an
// "(active)" marker for the current context. Errors are swallowed because
// completion runs on every TAB press; a failed read just yields no suggestions.
func completeContextNames(_ *cobra.Command, args []string, _ string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
	if len(args) != 0 {
		// <context> is a single positional; nothing to complete past it.
		return nil, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
	}
	all, current, err := auth.Contexts()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
	}
	out := make([]string, 0, len(all))
	for _, c := range all {
		desc := c.Handle
		if c.CoreURL != "" {
			desc += " " + c.CoreURL
		}
		if c.Name == current {
			desc += " (active)"
		}
		out = append(out, c.Name+"\t"+desc)
	}
	return out, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
}

`org`/`repo`/`project`/`grant` now authenticate as the **active login context**
instead of always hitting the static default core — and refresh their token
silently.

## Why
After `entire auth use <ctx>`, control-plane commands ignored the switch: they
always dialed `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` (or the `us.auth.entire.io` default) and
resolved their token from a manager pinned to that host. So a context on a
different core was silently unused — the bug pattern `auth status` already fixed
in #1341, now extended to the rest of the control plane.

## What changed
- `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()` picks host + token from the active context,
  falling back to `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL`/default only when no context is active.
  The env var is a **fallback host, not an override** (a token from core B can't
  authenticate against core A), matching `auth status`.
- `coreapi.New()` resolves through it; the bearer comes from the per-context
  refreshing provider, so an expired token re-mints from the stored refresh
  token (the silent-refresh down payment on COR-389).
- Removed the now-stale `auth use` cross-core warning and updated its help.
- `docs/architecture/upstream-host-resolution.md`: the "one core + resource
  servers" model and the deferred data-API work.

## Effect
```
entire auth use <ctx-on-another-core>
entire org list      # now hits that context's core, with a silently-refreshed token
```

## Not in scope (next slice)
Data-API commands (`activity`/`search`/`trail`/`dispatch`) still target
`ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` and don't follow the context yet — that needs a
`/.well-known` on `entire.io` advertising its trusted cores + audience. Designed
in the doc.

## Test
Unit tests for the affected packages (`cli`, `auth`, `api`, `coreapi`) + lint
clean. Full `mise run test:ci` (integration + canary) not yet run — leaving that
to CI.

content.content:
19	// New returns a *Client wired to talk to the Entire control plane (Core
20	// API) as the currently logged-in user.
21	//
22	// The host and bearer come from auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget: the active
23	// contexts.json login's core (so `entire auth use <ctx>` retargets the
24	// control plane), or — when ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL is set or no context is
25	// active — the configured auth host. The Core API is served at
26	// <core>/api/v1. The bearer is resolved lazily per request; for an active
27	// context it re-mints silently from the stored refresh token, and for the
28	// static path an RFC 8693 exchange happens transparently when the stored
29	// token's audience doesn't cover the core.
30	func New() (*Client, error) {
31		target, err := auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()
32		if err != nil {
33			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve control-plane target: %w", err)
34		}
35		src := &providerSource{provide: target.TokenSource}
36		client, err := NewClient(strings.TrimRight(target.CoreURL, "/")+apiBasePath, src)
37		if err != nil {
38			return nil, fmt.Errorf("build core API client: %w", err)
39		}
40		return client, nil
41	}
42	
43	// NewWithBearer returns a *Client targeting an explicit core origin with a
44	// fixed bearer token — no per-request resolution or STS exchange. Used when a
45	// command must hit a specific login server rather than the configured
46	// AuthBaseURL: e.g. `entire auth status` querying /me on the active context's
47	// core with that context's session token.
48	func NewWithBearer(coreBaseURL, token string) (*Client, error) {
49		base := strings.TrimRight(coreBaseURL, "/")
50		client, err := NewClient(base+apiBasePath, staticBearer{token: token})
51		if err != nil {
52			return nil, fmt.Errorf("build core API client: %w", err)
53		}
54		return client, nil
55	}
56	
57	// staticBearer is a SecuritySource that returns a fixed bearer token. Same
58	// sessionAuth-skipping rationale as bearerSource.
